title: FAR Module 6 — TBS 5

fields.label: Item 4 — Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities
Item 5 — Ending Net Assets With Donor Restrictions

html:
FINAL TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Comprehensive FAR Analysis

Complete the following independent year-end analyses using concepts from across the FAR section.

Part A — Financial Statement Adjustments

Meridian Company reports preliminary net income of $520,000.

  1. Salaries of $28,000 have been earned by employees but have not been recorded.
  2. Service revenue of $22,000 has been earned but not recorded.
  3. Depreciation expense of $35,000 has not been recorded.
  4. Ending inventory is understated by $8,000.

Item 1 — Adjusted Net Income

Part B — Accounts Receivable

Beginning Accounts Receivable was $160,000. Credit sales during the year were $850,000, and cash collected from customers was $805,000.

No receivables were written off during the year.

Item 2 — Ending Accounts Receivable

Part C — Bonds Payable

Bonds have a face amount of $800,000 and a beginning carrying amount of $760,000.

The stated annual interest rate is 5%, the effective annual rate is 7%, and interest is paid annually.

Item 3 — Ending Bond Carrying Amount

Part D — Statement of Cash Flows

A separate company reports:

  • Net income: $460,000
  • Depreciation expense: $55,000
  • Accounts Receivable increased: $18,000
  • Inventory decreased: $12,000
  • Accounts Payable decreased: $7,000

Item 4 — Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities

Part E — Not-for-Profit Accounting

An NFP begins the year with $40,000 of net assets with donor restrictions.

During the year, it receives an unconditional donor-restricted contribution of $125,000.

It incurs $80,000 of qualifying expenditures that satisfy donor restrictions.

Item 5 — Ending Net Assets With Donor Restrictions
explanation:
Item 1 — Adjusted Net Income

Preliminary Net Income: $520,000

− Accrued Salaries: $28,000

+ Accrued Revenue: $22,000

− Depreciation: $35,000

+ Inventory Correction: $8,000

Adjusted Net Income = $487,000

Item 2 — Ending Accounts Receivable

Beginning Accounts Receivable: $160,000

+ Credit Sales: $850,000

− Cash Collections: $805,000

Ending Accounts Receivable = $205,000

Item 3 — Ending Bond Carrying Amount

Beginning Carrying Amount: $760,000

Effective Interest Expense:

$760,000 × 7% = $53,200

Cash Interest:

$800,000 × 5% = $40,000

Discount Amortization:

$53,200 − $40,000 = $13,200

$760,000 + $13,200

Ending Carrying Amount = $773,200

Item 4 — Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities

Net Income: $460,000

+ Depreciation: $55,000

− Increase in Accounts Receivable: $18,000

+ Decrease in Inventory: $12,000

− Decrease in Accounts Payable: $7,000

Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities = $502,000

Item 5 — Net Assets With Donor Restrictions

Beginning Net Assets With Donor Restrictions: $40,000

+ Donor-Restricted Contribution: $125,000

− Restrictions Satisfied: $80,000

Ending Net Assets With Donor Restrictions = $85,000

Final FAR Integration

This simulation combines adjusting entries, receivable rollforwards, effective-interest amortization, operating cash flow, and NFP donor-restriction accounting.

On cumulative FAR problems, identify the accounting model first, calculate each component separately, and only then combine the effects.
